home_faq_a1: No. Shaking sticks, casting moon blocks and reading verdicts are all free. If you want to go deeper, you can ask Yue Lao for an in-depth reading (US$2.99 once, tax included): pay once, keep it forever, never auto-renews.
home_faq_a2: No sign-in is needed to draw a stick; the sticks you shake are stored only on your own phone or computer. To save in-depth readings or make a wish at the Wishing Pond, sign in with a code sent to your email — no password.
home_faq_a3: A "no" cast means Yue Lao isn't answering this time. Pause, think again about what you want to ask, and feel free to come back in a few days.
home_faq_a4: Switch languages from the menu at the top right. The English site is a machine-translated draft still under review: interface, verdicts, readings and card meanings are in English, while stick verses keep their original Chinese with an English gloss.
home_faq_a5: A stick isn't a prophecy — it helps you think through what's on your mind. You've already read the free verdict; whether it rings true, you'll know.
home_faq_a6: The verses weren't written by us. They are the long-circulated 100 Yue Lao temple verses, which borrow lines from classical texts (the Book of Songs, the Analects, Mencius, Romance of the Western Chamber and more); each has been checked against its source and cited. The verdicts were newly written by us for three kinds of questions: about them, finding love, and getting back together.
